questions.topic: A sector area from a central angle
questions.stem: Revision problem 4 asks which formula gives sector area.

options.text: pi r squared divided by theta

questions.explanation: Sector area is the fraction theta/360 of the full circle area. The formula uses pi r squared scaled by the angle fraction.

questions.topic: An arc length from a central angle
questions.learningObjective: Diagnose arc length using area formula
questions.stem: Revision problem 11 uses circle area instead of circumference for arc length.

options.text: Arc length is angle fraction of circumference, not area
Area formula is fine for large angles

questions.explanation: Arc length = (theta/360)*2*pi*r. Using pi*r^2 computes a sector area, not a length.

questions.topic: A chord length from a central angle
questions.stem: Revision problem 18 asks why chord length uses 2r sin(theta/2).

answer.exemplar: The chord is the base of an isosceles triangle with sides r, so dropping a perpendicular bisects the angle and chord equals 2r sin(theta/2).

questions.explanation: Splitting the isosceles triangle creates a right triangle with hypotenuse r and opposite side half the chord.

questions.topic: A diagonal count derived combinatorially
questions.stem: Revision problem 22: how many diagonals in a hexagon?
questions.explanation: Diagonals = n(n-3)/2 = 6*3/2 = 9. Each vertex connects to n-3 others, halved to avoid double counting.

questions.topic: A volume formula for a prism
questions.stem: Revision problem 31: prism base area 14, height 5; find volume.
questions.explanation: Volume = base area * height = 14*5 = 70. Prism volume scales linearly with height.

questions.topic: A volume formula for a pyramid
questions.stem: Revision problem 47 asks which formula gives pyramid volume.

options.text: One half times base area times height
One third times base area times height

questions.explanation: A pyramid tapers to a point, so volume is one third base area times height. Base times height is for prisms.

questions.topic: A surface area including both bases
questions.learningObjective: Identify surface area with both bases
questions.stem: Revision problem 8 asks which net includes both bases for surface area.

options.text: A pyramid net with one base only
A prism net with two bases and lateral rectangles
A cone net with one circular base

questions.explanation: A prism has two parallel bases, so its net includes both. Pyramids and cones have one base.

questions.topic: A sphere and its surface area
questions.stem: Revision problem 15 uses 4 pi r cubed for sphere surface area.

options.text: Surface area is 4 pi r squared, not cubed
Cubed is correct for surface area
Surface area equals 2 pi r squared
Surface area equals pi r squared

questions.explanation: Sphere surface area = 4*pi*r^2. Cubing gives volume (4/3*pi*r^3), not area.

questions.topic: A composite solid broken into parts
questions.stem: Revision problem 29 asks how to find volume of a composite solid.

answer.exemplar: Break the solid into simple parts such as prisms and cylinders, compute each volume, then add or subtract as needed, keeping units consistent.

questions.explanation: Decomposition turns a complex solid into familiar pieces. Add volumes of included parts and subtract removed ones.

questions.topic: A volume formula for a cylinder
questions.stem: Revision problem 36: cylinder radius 3, height 7; find volume.
questions.explanation: Volume = pi*r^2*h = pi*9*7 = 197.92. Base area times height gives cylinder volume.

questions.topic: A Pythagorean theorem in space
questions.learningObjective: Compute space diagonal of a box
questions.stem: Revision problem 43: box 3 by 4 by 12; find space diagonal.
questions.explanation: sqrt(3^2+4^2+12^2)=13. The space diagonal combines all three edge lengths.

questions.topic: A coordinate after a rotation
questions.stem: Revision problem 50 rotates point (1,0) 90 degrees about origin.
questions.explanation: A 90-degree counterclockwise rotation sends (x,y) to (-y,x), so (1,0) becomes (0,1).

questions.topic: A map scale and a real distance
questions.stem: Revision problem 1 asks what a 1:50000 map scale means.

options.text: 50000 cm on map equals 1 cm in reality
1 cm on map equals 50000 square cm
The map is 50000 times larger than reality
1 cm on map equals 50000 cm in reality

questions.explanation: A 1:50000 scale means one unit on the map represents 50000 of the same units in reality.

questions.topic: A scale model and its ratio
questions.stem: Revision problem 23 inverts a 1:200 model ratio.

options.text: Ratio does not matter for models
The ratio should be squared for models

questions.explanation: A 1:200 model ratio means one model unit equals 200 real units. Inverting it makes the model larger than reality.

questions.topic: Writing a sector area expression
questions.stem: Revision problem 5 asks how to write a sector area expression.

answer.exemplar: Multiply the circle area pi r squared by the fraction theta over 360 to get the sector area expression, where theta is the central angle.

questions.explanation: The angle fraction scales the full circle area. Writing pi r squared alone omits the angle.

questions.topic: Writing an arc length expression
questions.stem: Revision problem 12: r=6, theta=60; write arc length value.
questions.explanation: Arc length = (60/360)*2*pi*6 = 6.283. The angle fraction scales the circumference.

questions.topic: Writing a chord length expression
questions.stem: Revision problem 19: r=5, theta=60; find chord length.
questions.explanation: Chord = 2*5*sin(30°) = 5. The half-angle sine gives half the chord.

questions.topic: Writing a diagonal count
questions.stem: Revision problem 26 asks which expression counts diagonals.
questions.explanation: Each vertex connects to n-3 nonadjacent vertices; halving avoids double counting. n(n-3)/2 is correct.

questions.topic: Writing a pyramid volume expression
questions.stem: Revision problem 33 asks which expression is pyramid volume.

options.text: One half times base area times height
One third times base area times height

questions.explanation: Pyramid volume is one third base area times height. The factor accounts for tapering to an apex.

questions.topic: Writing a cone curved area
questions.stem: Revision problem 40 uses pi r squared for cone curved area.

options.text: Curved area is pi r l, not pi r squared
pi r squared is correct for curved area
options.misconception: confuses base area with curved area

options.text: Curved area equals 2 pi r l
Curved area equals pi r squared h

questions.explanation: Cone curved (lateral) area = pi*r*l. pi*r^2 is the base area, not the side.

questions.topic: A sector area from a central angle
questions.stem: Revision problem 2 asks why sector area uses theta over 360.

answer.exemplar: A sector is a fraction of the circle, and theta over 360 gives that fraction of the full circle area because the full circle is 360 degrees.

questions.explanation: The central angle determines what fraction of the circle the sector covers. Multiplying by circle area gives sector area.

questions.topic: An arc length from a central angle
questions.stem: Revision problem 9: r=4, theta=90; find arc length.
questions.explanation: Arc length = (90/360)*2*pi*4 = 6.283. The angle fraction scales the circumference.

questions.topic: A chord length from a central angle
questions.stem: Revision problem 16: r=8, theta=60; find chord length.
questions.explanation: Chord = 2*8*sin(30°) = 8. The half-angle sine gives half the chord.

questions.topic: A diagonal count derived combinatorially
questions.stem: Revision problem 24: how many diagonals in an octagon?
questions.explanation: 8*(8-3)/2 = 20. Each vertex connects to 5 others, halved to avoid double counting.

questions.topic: A volume formula for a prism
questions.stem: Revision problem 30 asks which formula gives prism volume.

options.text: Base area times height divided by 3

questions.explanation: Prism volume is base area times height. The one-third factor is for pyramids.

questions.topic: A volume formula for a pyramid
questions.stem: Revision problem 37 computes pyramid volume as base area times height.

options.text: Pyramid volume needs one third of base area times height
Base times height is correct for pyramids
Pyramid volume is base area times height squared

questions.explanation: A pyramid tapers to a point, so volume is one third base area times height. Base times height is the prism formula.

questions.topic: A surface area including both bases
questions.stem: Revision problem 44 asks why a prism surface area includes both bases.

answer.exemplar: A prism has two congruent bases, and surface area covers every face, so both bases must be included in the total along with lateral faces.

questions.explanation: Surface area sums all faces. A prism has two bases, so omitting one understates the area.

questions.topic: A sphere and its surface area
questions.stem: Revision problem 10: sphere radius 3; find surface area.
questions.explanation: Surface area = 4*pi*3^2 = 113.1. The radius is squared, not cubed.

questions.topic: A composite solid broken into parts
questions.stem: Revision problem 34: cylinder radius 2, height 5, minus cone same base height 5; find volume.
questions.explanation: Cylinder volume = pi*4*5 = 62.832; cone = (1/3)*pi*4*5 = 20.944; difference = 41.888.

questions.topic: A volume formula for a cylinder
questions.stem: Revision problem 38 asks which formula gives cylinder volume.
questions.explanation: Cylinder volume is base area pi*r^2 times height. 2*pi*r*h is lateral surface area.

questions.topic: A Pythagorean theorem in space
questions.stem: Revision problem 42 asks for space diagonal of a box.

options.misconception: adds lengths instead of using Pythagorean

options.text: Square root of sum of squares of three edges

questions.explanation: The space diagonal is sqrt(a^2+b^2+c^2). Sum or product of edges gives different quantities.

questions.topic: A coordinate after a rotation
questions.stem: Revision problem 49 rotates (0,1) 90 degrees counterclockwise and gets (1,0).
questions.explanation: Counterclockwise 90 maps (x,y) to (-y,x), so (0,1) becomes (-1,0). The given result is wrong.

questions.topic: A map scale and a real distance
questions.stem: Revision problem 5 asks how to convert map distance to real distance.

answer.exemplar: Multiply the map distance by the scale denominator to get the real distance, keeping units consistent, so 1 cm becomes 50000 cm at 1:50000.

questions.explanation: The scale denominator converts map units to real units. Multiplying applies the ratio directly.

questions.topic: A scale model and its ratio
questions.stem: Revision problem 20: model length 4 cm at 1:200; find real length.
questions.explanation: Real length = 4*200 = 800 cm. The scale denominator converts model to real.

questions.topic: Writing a sector area expression
questions.stem: Revision problem 27: r=6, theta=60; find sector area.
questions.explanation: Sector area = (60/360)*pi*36 = 18.85. The angle fraction is one sixth.

questions.topic: Writing an arc length expression
questions.stem: Revision problem 35 asks which expression gives arc length.
questions.explanation: Arc length is the angle fraction of circumference. Using circle area gives sector area, not length.

questions.topic: Writing a chord length expression
questions.stem: Revision problem 41 asks which expression gives chord length.

options.misconception: uses full angle and single radius

questions.explanation: Chord length = 2*r*sin(theta/2). The half-angle sine gives half the chord in the right triangle.

questions.topic: Writing a diagonal count
questions.stem: Revision problem 45 counts n(n-1)/2 for diagonals.
questions.explanation: n(n-1)/2 counts all pairs, including sides. Subtracting 3 per vertex removes sides, giving n(n-3)/2.

questions.topic: Writing a pyramid volume expression
questions.stem: Revision problem 46 asks why pyramid volume has a one-third factor.

answer.exemplar: A pyramid fills one third of the prism with the same base and height, so its volume expression includes one third of base area times height.

questions.explanation: The tapering to an apex reduces volume to one third of the corresponding prism. The factor reflects that geometry.

questions.topic: Writing a cone curved area
questions.stem: Revision problem 48: cone r=3, l=5; find curved area.
questions.explanation: Curved area = pi*3*5 = 47.124. The slant height, not vertical height, is used.

questions.topic: A sector area from a central angle
questions.stem: Revision problem 3: r=5, theta=72; find sector area.
questions.explanation: Sector area = (72/360)*pi*25 = 15.708. The angle fraction is one fifth.

questions.topic: An arc length from a central angle
questions.stem: Revision problem 13 asks which expression gives arc length.
questions.explanation: Arc length is the angle fraction of circumference. Using circle area gives sector area, not length.

questions.topic: A chord length from a central angle
questions.stem: Revision problem 17 asks which expression gives chord length.

options.misconception: uses full angle and single radius

questions.explanation: Chord length = 2*r*sin(theta/2). The half-angle sine gives half the chord in the right triangle.

questions.topic: A diagonal count derived combinatorially
questions.stem: Revision problem 21 counts n(n-2)/2 for diagonals.
questions.explanation: n(n-2)/2 counts sides as diagonals. Subtracting 3 per vertex removes sides, giving n(n-3)/2.

questions.topic: A volume formula for a prism
questions.stem: Revision problem 28 asks why prism volume is base area times height.

answer.exemplar: A prism has constant cross-section, so volume is base area stacked through the height, giving base area times height with no tapering along the height.

questions.explanation: Constant cross-section means every slice has the same area. Multiplying by height gives volume.

questions.topic: A volume formula for a pyramid
questions.stem: Revision problem 32: pyramid base area 18, height 6; find volume.
questions.explanation: Volume = (1/3)*18*6 = 36. The one-third factor accounts for tapering.
questions.hint: One third of base times height.

questions.topic: A surface area including both bases
questions.stem: Revision problem 4: prism base side 4, height 5; find surface area.
questions.explanation: Two bases contribute 32 and lateral area contributes 80, totaling 112.

questions.topic: A sphere and its surface area
questions.stem: Revision problem 14 asks which formula gives sphere surface area.
questions.explanation: Sphere surface area = 4*pi*r^2. Cubing gives volume, and 2*pi*r^2 is a hemisphere.

questions.topic: A composite solid broken into parts
questions.stem: Revision problem 25 asks how to find volume of a composite solid.

options.text: Decompose into simple solids and sum or subtract volumes

questions.explanation: Decomposition breaks a complex solid into familiar pieces. Sum or subtract their volumes as needed.

questions.topic: A volume formula for a cylinder
questions.stem: Revision problem 39 uses 2 pi r h for cylinder volume.

options.text: 2 pi r h is lateral area, not volume
2 pi r h is correct for volume
Cylinder volume is pi r h
Cylinder volume is 2 pi r squared

questions.explanation: 2*pi*r*h is lateral surface area. Volume is base area pi*r^2 times height.

questions.topic: A Pythagorean theorem in space
questions.stem: Revision problem 41 asks why space diagonal squares three edges.

answer.exemplar: The space diagonal forms the hypotenuse of a right triangle whose legs are one edge and the diagonal of the base, so all three squared edges sum under one square root.

questions.explanation: Applying Pythagorean twice combines all three edges. Squaring and summing gives the straight-line distance through the box.

questions.topic: A coordinate after a rotation
questions.stem: Revision problem 47: rotate (2,3) 90 degrees counterclockwise; find x-coordinate.
questions.explanation: Counterclockwise 90 maps (x,y) to (-y,x), so x becomes -3. The y-coordinate becomes 2.

questions.topic: A map scale and a real distance
questions.stem: Revision problem 7: map distance 3 cm at 1:25000; find real km.
questions.explanation: Real = 3*25000 = 75000 cm = 0.75 km. Convert centimeters to kilometers.

questions.topic: A scale model and its ratio
questions.stem: Revision problem 22 asks which ratio means 1 cm model = 5 m real.
questions.explanation: 1 cm to 5 m = 1 cm to 500 cm = 1:500. Units must match before forming the ratio.

questions.topic: Writing a sector area expression
questions.stem: Revision problem 6 asks which expression gives sector area.

options.text: pi r squared divided by theta

questions.explanation: Sector area is the angle fraction of circle area. The formula scales pi*r^2 by theta/360.

questions.topic: Writing an arc length expression
questions.stem: Revision problem 15 uses pi r squared instead of 2 pi r in arc length.

options.text: Arc length uses circumference 2 pi r, not area
Area formula is fine for arcs

questions.explanation: Arc length = (theta/360)*2*pi*r. Using pi*r^2 computes a sector area, not a length.

questions.topic: Writing a chord length expression
questions.stem: Revision problem 18 asks why chord length uses sine of half angle.

answer.exemplar: Bisecting the central angle creates a right triangle with hypotenuse r and opposite side half the chord, so chord equals 2r sin(theta/2).

questions.explanation: The half-angle sine relates the radius to half the chord. Doubling gives the full chord length.

questions.topic: Writing a diagonal count
questions.stem: Revision problem 23: polygon has 10 sides; find diagonals.
questions.explanation: 10*(10-3)/2 = 35. Each vertex connects to 7 others, halved to avoid double counting.

questions.topic: Writing a pyramid volume expression
questions.stem: Revision problem 31: pyramid base area 24, height 9; find volume.
questions.explanation: Volume = (1/3)*24*9 = 72. The one-third factor accounts for tapering.
questions.hint: One third of base times height.

questions.topic: Writing a cone curved area
questions.stem: Revision problem 36 asks which expression gives cone curved area.
questions.explanation: Cone curved area = pi*r*l. Base area and cylinder formulas give different quantities.
